mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates easy monetary conditions, which may stimulate borrowing and investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is low but SPX returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases but SPX returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates increased construction activity and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but SPX returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment and increasing payroll employment signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE is low and PAYEMS increases but SPX returns are not positive (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in federal funds rate may lead to decreased borrowing and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases but SPX returns are positive more than 65% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in federal funds rate may signal tighter monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases sharply but SPX returns are positive more than 65% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases but SPX returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases but SPX returns are negative more than 35% of the time.
